observations.behavior: Documentation update: the description for the transactional email workflow tool was changed, replacing the word 'Workflow' with 'Transactional email' in the instruction to set an API key. No implementation or test changes are supplied.
observations.code_quote: "description": "Step 1 of 2 for make email template transactional. Validates the arguments and returns a signed confirmation_hash plus a message to surface to the user. The user must reply with the literal word \"confirm\" before you call the matching -execute tool with the hash. Original action: Make an email template sendable from code with one API call, for emails a person triggers such as password resets, receipts and sign-in codes. This is one-way: the template can't be made non-transactional again. Transactional sends ignore marketing opt-outs, so never use this for marketing email. The template needs a subject and a body, and the project needs a verified email sender (pass from_integration_id to pick one, otherwise the project's default sender is used). Requires human typed confirmation. The response has transactional_hog_flow_id, the workflow that sends the email. Share the template's _posthogUrl so the user can review and publish it. Then tell the user what is left: create a project secret API key with Transactional email set to Write, and send from their backend with posthog.emails.send in the Node.js or Python SDK, or POST /api/projects/@current/messaging/send/email/ with template.id in the body. Each send returns a message ID, and posthog.emails.get or GET /api/projects/@current/messaging/emails/{message_id}/ reads its status.",
observations.posthog_connection: This could support a workflow where a user creates a transactional email API key, but the implementation and tests are not supplied.
